name: WEDCO
old_description: This year, we proudly celebrate 75 years of delivering trusted solutions! Since 1950, WEDCO has been built on strong relationships and dedicated leadership. We’re especially grateful to the Elmore Family, whose vision and commitment guided us for decades. In 2008, we began transitioning ownership from the Elmores, and today, we’re proudly 100% employee-owned.
about:
WEDCO is headquartered in Reno, Nevada, and was founded in 1950 by the Elmore family. The company transitioned to employee ownership in 2008 and is now 100% employee-owned. It operates four locations across Northern Nevada: Reno, Fallon, Carson City, and Winnemucca.

The company operates as an electrical distributor and solutions provider, carrying over $10 million in inventory from brands such as Square D, Schneider Electric, Milwaukee Tool, Southwire, and Eaton. Its services include VFD programming and start-up, motor control training, project management, switchgear and lighting quotations, and technical training. The firm serves industrial automation, residential, commercial, utility, and mining markets.

WEDCO's customer base includes industrial pump contractors, residential and commercial electrical contractors, industrial automation and MRO buyers, mining operations, and utility companies. The distributor positions itself as a single source for electrical supplies across Northern Nevada.

The employee-owned structure is cited as a differentiator, aligning employee incentives with customer outcomes. The company emphasizes community involvement, supporting organizations like the University of Nevada, youth sports, and the Boys and Girls Club, and highlights reliable delivery, fast response, and expert project support as core values.

name: Wagner's Fabrication
old_description: If you’re in need of welding or metal fabrication services, our team is here to help. We’ve been providing the Colorado Springs area with welding solutions since 1988, and are ready to help you, no matter your location. Contact us below to get a consultation and to find out more about how we can help you on your project.
about:
Wagner's Fabrication operates from Colorado Springs, Colorado, where it was founded in 1988 as a family-owned welding and metal fabrication shop. The business remains family owned and operated, drawing on more than 50 years of combined experience among its team.

The shop specializes in precision TIG welding for medical and aerospace applications, along with custom metal fabrication ranging from small individual projects to large-scale production work. Services include precision medical welding, precision aerospace welding, and general custom fabrication, with the company noting that no project is too big or too small.

Customers span the medical device and aerospace sectors, as well as individual clients needing repairs such as stainless steel exhaust components, magnesium engine cases, and motorcycle frames. The company has served clients across Colorado and is beginning to expand its reach nationally.

Founded on a detailed, project-specific approach, Wagner's Fabrication emphasizes its family-owned structure and deep combined experience as differentiators in a market where it aims to stand apart from other local welders.

name: Walker Woodworking | Manufacturing Plant
old_description: Since 2000, Walker Woodworking has established a reputation for quality craftsmanship, exceptional service, and a commitment to providing the finest materials, the latest innovations, and the best cabinet designs for your home or business. When you choose our custom cabinets, you have access to a range of options that other cabinet makers cannot offer.
about:
Walker Woodworking was founded in 2000 in Shelby, North Carolina, by Travis Walker, beginning as a hobby and growing into a team of skilled craftsmen building one-of-a-kind cabinets. The company operates a 75,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Shelby.

The shop produces custom cabinets, fine furniture, and luxury cabinetry for residential and commercial spaces. Core processes include custom cabinet manufacturing, CNC routing, extrusion preparation for integrated lighting, and aluminum extrusion machining in silver or black finishes. The facility also handles lighting installation and testing, though it does not warrant third-party electrical work. A service and repair department supports existing installations.

Customers include homeowners, interior designers, and builders across the Southeast. Projects range from kitchen and bath cabinetry to built-in furniture for offices and hospitality venues. The company works with client-supplied extrusion samples and confirms machinability before production.

Walker Woodworking emphasizes in-house production to adapt quickly to design changes and sustainable practices woven through material selection and fabrication. The founder’s original focus on craftsmanship and service remains the basis for the company’s approach to custom millwork.

name: Wallace Woodworks Artisans LLC
old_description: Founded in 1982 by Jeff Wallace, Wallace Woodworks has developed a reputation for dependability and quality workmanship by providing exceptional value to those desiring unsurpassed quality. Based in Salt Lake City, Wallace Woodworks has completed projects locally in Utah as well as nationwide.
about:
Wallace Woodworks Artisans LLC was founded in 1982 by Jeff Wallace in South Salt Lake, Utah. The shop began as a one-man operation and grew through word-of-mouth referrals into a team of craftsmen producing custom woodwork for clients across the United States.

The company specializes in bespoke architectural millwork, including kitchen cabinetry, bathroom vanities, custom furniture, and architectural details such as carved panels and built-ins. Projects are designed in-house and fabricated using traditional joinery and modern woodworking equipment, with each piece tailored to the client’s specifications. The workshop handles everything from initial consultation and design through final installation.

Wallace Woodworks serves residential homeowners, interior designers, architects, and builders. Notable projects include a private club room with custom carvings, office cabinetry, and whole-home kitchen and bath installations for clients in Utah and beyond. The firm’s portfolio shows work in both new construction and renovation contexts.

The company’s founding principle, reflected in a Frank Lloyd Wright quote displayed on its site, is that “quality is remembered long after price is forgotten.” Wallace Woodworks emphasizes dependability, attention to detail, and the use of premium materials as its primary differentiators in a market often driven by cost.

about:
Walt Palmer Supply, Inc. was founded in 1958 in Salt Lake City, Utah, as a family-owned business. Now in its second generation of family ownership, the company has served Utah supply houses, contractors, and homeowners for over six decades.

The company operates a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility producing sheet metal components for HVAC, plumbing, and roofing applications. Its product lines include square and round HVAC duct, water heater pans and venting for plumbing, and roof jacks, flashings, curbs, and caps for roofing. Custom design and fabrication services are also offered to meet specific project requirements.

Walt Palmer Supply primarily serves the HVAC, plumbing, and roofing sectors within the construction industry. Its customer base consists of Utah-based supply houses, mechanical and roofing contractors, and residential homeowners seeking replacement parts or custom solutions.

The company emphasizes its commitment to quality, on-time delivery, and efficiency, rooted in a tradition of family ownership since 1958. It differentiates itself through its manufacturing capabilities, custom design flexibility, and long-standing relationships with local trade professionals.

name: Wapsie Valley Creamery
old_description: Wapsie has successfully produced products in the dairy industry since 1906.  Although the dairy industry has shown little growth over the years, Wapsie has continuously adjusted its manufacturing processes and equipment to compete in the volatile landscapes of the dairy industry.  Wapsie Valley Creamery continues to invest in new equipment that is able to process more milk more efficiently to obtain the best yields in its products.  Although the company has grown over the years, the company is still a relatively small company in the dairy industry.
about:
Wapsie Valley Creamery, a family-owned dairy processor, has operated in Independence, Iowa since 1906. The company began as a small creamery and has remained under family ownership through multiple generations.

At its Independence plant, Wapsie manufactures cheese, lactose, and whey products, processing milk sourced from more than 170 independent dairy farms across eastern Iowa, southwestern Wisconsin, and northwestern Illinois. The facility employs approximately 140 people and has continually upgraded its equipment to increase throughput and improve yield.

The creamery sells its cheese in bulk to large wholesale companies that cut and shred it for private-label retail packages. Its lactose goes to food manufacturers for use in confectionery, sweeteners, and dairy blends, while reduced-lactose whey is supplied to wholesalers for processed cheeses, cheese spreads, and calf milk replacer.

Wapsie emphasizes a quality system that starts with farm-level inspections by state and federal agencies, supplemented by its own field staff and a dedicated quality-assurance laboratory. The company says its long history and ongoing investment in processing technology allow it to maintain consistent product standards despite its relatively small size in the industry.

name: Ward's Manufacturing
old_description: Founded by siblings Kiffin and Kelly Ward, the company is committed to domestic manufacturing and building long-term partnerships by delivering high-quality, made-in-USA parts with unmatched flexibility.
about:
Ward's Manufacturing operates from Warren, Rhode Island, where siblings Kiffin and Kelly Ward founded the company in 2022. The woman-owned, millennial-owned business began after the pair experienced firsthand the difficulties of sourcing reliable domestic metal fabrication and decided to fill that gap themselves, drawing on a family legacy of tradespeople and a commitment to U.S.-based production.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication including fiber laser cutting, CNC press brake bending, machining, finishing, and product design. Its equipment includes a 3 kW fiber optic laser with a 5-by-10-foot bed capable of cutting mild steel up to 3/4 inch, stainless up to 3/8 inch, and aluminum up to 5/16 inch, plus a 190-ton CNC press brake that bends parts up to 10 feet long. In-house finishing covers #4 brushed, vibratory tumbling, glass bead blasting, and orbital sanding, while value-added services range from powder coating and anodizing to welding, assembly, and heat treating. The company reports a 99% quality rate and handles orders from single prototypes to production runs of tens of thousands of units with no minimum order quantity.

Ward's serves customers across aerospace and defense, marine, robotics and automation, renewable energy (solar frames, wind turbine components), medical devices, electronics enclosures, and industrial equipment. Concrete examples include aircraft components, marine-grade corrosion-resistant parts, robotic sensor components, solar panel frames, wind energy parts, medical-grade metal parts, and electronic enclosures and brackets. The company has shipped to 43 U.S. states and four Canadian provinces.

The founders started the business to address the lack of responsive, high-quality domestic fabrication options they encountered as buyers. They emphasize short lead times — including 24- to 48-hour expedited delivery — flexible scheduling, responsive communication, and the supply-chain security of all-U.S. production. Woman-owned (WBE-certified) and Green Manufacturer certifications help clients meet supplier diversity and sustainability goals.

name: Warwick Mills Inc
old_description: Warwick specializes in weaving high-strength polyester, nylon, and polypropylene fibers. We are also experts in adhesion, using custom RFL and isocyanate formulas to bond textiles and rubber based upon your application's individual requirements.
about:
Warwick Mills operates from New Ipswich, New Hampshire, where it has maintained a 135-plus year history in fabric engineering. Ownership details such as family or veteran status are not stated in available sources.

The company specializes in engineering technical textiles for protective applications. Its core capabilities include custom weaving of high-strength polyester, nylon, and polypropylene fibers; textile lamination; custom adhesive formulation using RFL and isocyanate chemistries; and performance coating. Warwick integrates research, development, testing, and full-scale manufacturing to produce custom roll goods, fabric laminates, chemical-biological barriers, fabrics for inflatable structures, and flexible composite materials.

Warwick serves the safety, aerospace, and outdoor industries, as well as the bicycle tire sector. A noted partnership with European manufacturer Bohle produced the TurtleSkin High Density Guard material used in Schwalbe tires such as the Ultremo, Marathon Supreme, and DD Racing Ralph lines. The company's materials engineers work directly with customers on design specifications and system development.

Warwick emphasizes a cooperative development philosophy that combines engineering and manufacturing under one roof. It states that designing with manufacturing in mind yields a seamless development strategy with shorter production times. The firm highlights its integrated development and manufacturing capabilities as a unique advantage in the protective textiles industry, backed by ISO 9001:2015 certification.

name: Waukesha-Pearce Industries (WPI)
old_description: Waukesha-Pearce Industries is a custom manufacturer and distributor of power generation equipment and parts, including low- and medium-voltage switchgear. Serves utility and industrial power generation markets; offers repair and maintenance of switchgear.
about:
Waukesha-Pearce Industries (WPI) was founded in 1924 in Bakersfield, California, by Louis Pearce Sr. The company remains family-owned, now in its fourth generation, and began with a vision to prioritize employee and customer needs to build lasting loyalty.

WPI operates as a custom manufacturer and distributor of power generation equipment, producing low- and medium-voltage switchgear, generator accessories, and related parts. It also runs a Construction & Mining Division that sells and services heavy equipment from brands, offering field and shop service, preventive maintenance, real-time fleet telematics, undercarriage repair, and welding and fabrication. The Engine Division provides compression and onshore drilling support equipment, along with build-to-suit power generation solutions. The company employs 200–499 people across multiple locations.

WPI serves utilities, industrial power generation, oil and gas, construction, mining, paving, and drilling sectors. Its customers include utility companies needing switchgear maintenance, industrial facilities requiring standby power, and construction firms relying on equipment service and telematics.

The company traces its differentiation to Louis Pearce Sr.’s founding commitment to care for employees and customers, a philosophy sustained through four generations. WPI emphasizes its core values and culture, aiming to deliver “The People. The Parts. The Equipment. To Keep You Moving.”

old_description: Wayne Mills has been weaving quality cotton products since 1910. Cotton webbing remains a core part of our business today. We maintain a large inventory of narrow cotton webbing which enables us to rapidly customize your product and quickly deliver finished goods. The experienced staff at our
about:
Wayne Mills has operated in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania since 1910. The family-owned business, now in its fifth generation, began weaving twill tapes and light webbings when steam was coal-fired and yarn arrived by horse-drawn wagon.

Today the company runs a 150,000-square-foot complex of nine buildings on four acres in the city's historic Germantown district. More than 60 employees—many with decades of tenure—operate warping and weaving machines, a high-speed bleaching range, a computer-controlled Mageba continuous dye line, and 16 skein dyeing machines. The facility also houses custom coating, reflective lamination, and cutting/packaging lines. Stock items such as cotton tapes (styles 6210, 5541, 5526, 4214, 5533) ship quickly, while custom orders are fulfilled with the same attention to detail.

The narrow fabrics serve apparel, bag and strap makers, military-specification programs, and safety applications requiring reflective lamination. Customers include Analog Watch Company and public-sector buyers such as the Philadelphia Commerce Department.

Wayne Mills differentiates itself with a 15-pound minimum for custom dye lots—far below the industry's typical 500- to 1,000-pound threshold—and an in-house quality lab that tests break strength, elongation, wash fastness, and adhesive performance. Environmental awards recognize its wastewater treatment, and the firm emphasizes U.S. manufacturing.
